# Exact limitation of centroid-leaf midpoint certificates

The additive midpoint lemma is valid, but its basic tree construction does not by itself prove OC.

Take n=1,d=3. Let K be a two-dimensional simplex of area one, with centroid g. Define three full-dimensional continuous fibers

F_-=[-2,2] x K,
F_0=[-5/4,11/4] x K,
F_+=[-1/2,1/2] x K,

at integer coordinates -1,0,1, and let C be the convex hull of these three fibers in R x R^3. This is a full-dimensional convex body. Its projection is [-1,1], so there are no other integer fibers. The endpoint fibers are exact because their base points are projection vertices. The middle fiber is exact because

(F_-+F_+)/2=[-5/4,5/4] x K subset F_0;

every convex combination projecting to zero is a mixture of F_0 and this endpoint average.

The three fiber volumes are 4,4,1, and total mixed volume is M=9. No fiber is heavy for n=1, since 4<9/2. The exact target unnormalized depth is

(gamma_3/2)M=(27/64)(9/2)=243/128.

At the centroid of any one fiber, its own-fiber halfspace capacity is at most its volume times gamma_2=4/9: use a halfspace acting only on the simplex factor K and attaining its sharp centroid cut. Thus every centroid-leaf certificate, even if improved from the ordinary gamma_3 estimate to the exact own-fiber capacity, has value at most

4gamma_2=16/9<243/128.

Among these three distinct integer fibers, the only midpoint operation producing a different available integer fiber combines -1 and 1 to produce 0. Their centroid average is the point (0,0,g), whose continuous interval coordinate is zero. The middle fiber's own-fiber capacity at this point is at most 5/4, as certified by the cut in the interval coordinate t<=0. The smaller endpoint's own-fiber capacity at its centroid is at most gamma_2=4/9. Therefore the basic additive midpoint rule k_root+min(b_left,b_right), even granting exact node capacities, yields at most

5/4+4/9=61/36<243/128.

No deeper distinct-label binary tree is available with only these three fibers. Thus optimizing all centroid-leaf single-fiber and basic midpoint-tree certificates cannot reach the OC target for this example.

This is not a counterexample to OC, nor does it rule out stronger correlated cap estimates, different leaf points, use of the unused part of an actual midpoint fiber, or other certificate rules. It identifies exactly the extra ingredient needed beyond the proved elementary midpoint addition. The midpoint fiber's actual centroid has interval coordinate 3/4, so it cannot be substituted for the averaged endpoint centroids while retaining the midpoint relation.
